slides.title: Ceramic or steel skate bearings?
slides.sub: Pick the right set for how you skate

slides.title: Race seriously? Ceramic earns it
slides.body: Ceramic balls are lighter and harder than steel. They spin up faster, run cooler and hold their speed deeper into a long effort.

slides.title: Train most days? Buy good steel
slides.body: A precision steel set still rolls beautifully, costs less and leaves you budget for wheels.

slides.title: Most skate ceramic is hybrid
slides.caption: Hybrid bearings run ceramic balls in steel races, so oil and dry storage still matter.

slides.title: Ceramic still needs oil
slides.body: The races and cage still need lubrication. A dry ceramic bearing feels slower than a clean, oiled steel set.

slides.title: Beginners: steel first
slides.body: Until technique and fitness hold you back, good steel gives most of the feel. Move to ceramic when your kit becomes the limit.
